title: Peace in the home
hook: a high value in Jewish family life

segments.voice: Yesterday's line was communities differ: these and these, argued honestly, each side taught fairly. Today, the smallest community there is: one home.

Sarah is inside the tent, listening. Outside, a guest tells Abraham that by this time next year, Sarah will have a son. She laughs to herself. In the King James words, she says: "After I am waxed old shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also?" A verse later, God speaks to Abraham about that laugh and repeats what she said. Except the repeat is different. Listen closely, because today's word hides in the part that goes missing.
screen: `SARAH LAUGHS IN THE TENT.` → `"MY LORD BEING OLD ALSO."` → `GOD REPEATS IT, DIFFERENTLY.`

segments.voice: You met this page of Talmud in your first year; today, what it means for a home. When God tells Abraham what Sarah said, the King James has: "Shall I of a surety bear a child, which am old?" Sarah's age stays in. Abraham's is gone. She had said, my lord is old too; God reports only, I am old. The Talmud notices and draws a lesson: great is peace, for even the Holy One altered words for its sake. Nobody needs to carry every sharp word from one spouse to the other. Peace is also something you chase. Hillel taught: be among the disciples of Aaron, loving peace and pursuing peace. Tradition tells of Aaron going to each side of a quarrel separately, telling each how much the other regretted it, until they met and embraced. And it's small and daily. The Talmud asks: if you can afford only one light, for Shabbat or for Hanukkah, which comes first? The Shabbat lamp in the home, for the sake of shalom bayit: a lit house, where nobody trips in the dark and tempers don't flare. Peace starts with being able to see each other. Shalom bayit is not silence, and it's not keeping up appearances. Teachers of this value say clearly that it never asks anyone to stay where they are not safe. It means a home where people are gentle on purpose, choose their words with care, and keep making the first move toward each other.
screen: `THE WORDS GOD LEFT OUT.` · `LOVING PEACE, PURSUING PEACE.` · `A LAMP SO WE CAN SEE.` · `NOT SILENCE, NOT DANGER.` · then, large: `PEACE AT HOME.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind the people you live with, or those closest to you, and one small friction between you right now: a sharp word, a chore, a silence gone on a little long. Choose one small move toward peace, a kind word or a sharp sentence you decide not to pass along, and hold it until it feels doable. And if home is ever not safe, please reach out: local emergency help, or in the US, call or text 988.
Shalom bayit: peace in the home. Pursued, not waited for, and built from small choices, like the words God left out for Sarah and Abraham. Today's word.
Your line: peace at home. Somebody has to go after it first. Rest well.

howItsDone: Jewish tradition counts shalom bayit, peace in the home, as a high value in family life; teachers draw on texts like God's softened report of Sarah's words and Hillel's call to love and pursue peace.

fork.setup: Sarah laughed and said she was old, and that Abraham was old too. you're about to tell Abraham what she said. what do you say?
options: repeat every word, including the part about his age.
say only that she laughed because she is old.
tell him nothing about the laugh.
fork.reveal: God reports only Sarah's own age; the Talmud learns from this that even the Holy One altered words for the sake of peace.

chat.says: Isn't shalom bayit just keeping quiet so there's no fighting at home?
options: No, it's pursuing peace with gentle words, and it never asks anyone to stay unsafe.
Yes, it means never raising a problem, so the home always looks calm.
No, it's a blessing for a new house; it isn't about how people treat each other.
chat.meaning: Shalom bayit is pursued, like Aaron chasing peace, through gentle words and small acts; its teachers say it never asks anyone to stay where they are not safe.

Aaron.meaning: Moses' brother, remembered for pursuing peace

Hillel.meaning: a great sage who taught love of peace

notes: Genesis 18:12–13 quoted from the KJV; confirm wording. 'By this time next year' paraphrases Genesis 18:10 ('according to the time of life').
Yevamot 65b (also Bava Metzia 87a): 'great is peace, for even the Holy One altered [words] for its sake', learned from Genesis 18:12–13. Paraphrased; confirm.

Avot 1:12 (Hillel: be of the disciples of Aaron, loving peace and pursuing peace) paraphrased; Aaron making peace between quarreling parties from Avot de-Rabbi Natan 12, introduced as 'tradition tells'. Confirm.
Shabbat 23b: Shabbat lamp takes precedence over Hanukkah lamp because of shalom bayit. Confirm. 'Nobody trips in the dark and tempers don't flare' is an explanatory gloss (cf. Rashi); confirm.

Safety line: 'Teachers of this value say clearly that it never asks anyone to stay where they are not safe.' Included deliberately because shalom bayit has been misused to pressure people to stay in abusive homes; confirm the wording with a Keeper.
